name: Use the canonical catalog language from the context documents
description: The domain terms live in CONTEXT-MAP.md (the contexts and how they relate) and docs/contexts/<context>/CONTEXT.md (one glossary per context). Catalog and Inventory are written; others are added when their first seed starts. Use these terms exactly in code, docs and the UI, and check the glossary before adding a term. Keep the files current with the domain-modeling skill (~/.agents/skills/domain-modeling): a CONTEXT.md is only a glossary, with 1–2 sentence definitions and an Avoid list. docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md was never committed and is unavailable.

title: Save every change to part details as a new, complete revision
rationale: Each change to part details saves a new, complete revision that never changes afterwards, grouped in a Change with a reason. Commands carry the current revision they expect. Restoring adds a new revision, and a change that alters nothing is rejected. Supplier data, stock, scans and drafts never create revisions.

title: Keep a CAD item's identity, its stored bytes and its revisions separate
rationale: A CAD item keeps its identity over time. Its stored bytes are identified by their SHA-256, and each revision's hash covers its content and license. Source and license belong to one exact CAD item revision. Moving or copying stored bytes never creates a revision.

title: Keep verification and protection separate
rationale: Verification is permanent proof about one exact revision. Protection is an audited setting that blocks changes to a part or CAD item. To fix a protected item, remove the protection with a reason, revise it, verify the new revision, then protect it again. Authority is never a silent way around protection.

name: Binary-safe content addressing inside PocketBase hooks
description: $security.sha256 hashes text, so bytes that are not UTF-8 would hash wrongly. The CSV import sends blobs as base64 in the JSON command and infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_lib.js decodes and hashes them in pure JS before $filesystem.fileFromBytes, so blobs are checked and written in the same transaction; tooling/catalog-import test the_route_hashes_blob_bytes_exactly checks it against Rust's sha2 at 1, 55, 56, 63, 64, 119, 120 and 300,000 bytes (PocketBase cannot store an empty file, so the route refuses empty blobs, and it refuses a blob that no CAD item revision in the request uses). Canonical documents whose SHA-256 is their identity (revision snapshots) are stored in text fields with an explicit max (a TextField max of 0 means 5000), never json fields, so the hashed bytes round-trip. Shared hook code lives in a non-.pb.js file loaded with require(`${__hooks}/catalog_lib.js`) inside the handler.

title: Derive Catalog record IDs from content and compare CSV imports with stored state on the server
rationale: Every Catalog record ID is the first 15 hex digits of SHA-256('kicad-parts:<kind>:v1\n<key>') (part from IPN, CAD item from kind + LIB:NAME, CAD item revision from CAD item + snapshot hash, blob from its bytes' hash, Change and audit entry from the correlation ID), computed in crates/catalog/src/ids.rs and re-derived by the route, so re-imports find the same records without a mapping table; a stored record is reused only if its hash or key matches, otherwise 409 id_collision. A symbol's blob is the exact bytes of that one top-level symbol (its source keeps file path, file hash and byte range), so editing a neighbouring symbol does not revise it; footprints and 3D models are whole files. Manufacturer parts (main first) are part details, so adding, removing or reordering one makes a new revision; a part has one datasheet, and a substitutes.csv datasheet that is neither blank nor the part's is a substitutes-csv-datasheet-differs import problem. POST /api/catalog/csv-imports compares with stored state in one transaction, and a Change is made only when there is at least one new revision. Changed part details get a new revision only when the current revision's Change kind is csv-import, otherwise an import problem. Supplier part numbers, LCSC codes and prices stay in the revision's source, never in its part details. Replaced in part: when a run is recorded without a Change and when an import is a 422 noop are now in mx-c5e787; expected revisions and the checkout check are in mx-64c42a.

name: Catalog write guards and tamper tests
description: catalog_write_guards.pb.js refuses every create, update and delete of catalog_* records through the record API with 403, superusers included (onRecord*Request hooks), and every update or delete from server code (onRecordUpdate/onRecordDelete) except moving a part's current_revision to the revision saved right after it (same part, number+1, predecessor = old current). Collection drops in down migrations are not record deletes, so rollback still works. Tests that need a tampered record (ID-collision cases) stop the server, UPDATE data.db with rusqlite, and restart on the same data dir.

title: Each CSV import run records what the CSV said; the zero-loss report rebuilds the CSV from the latest run
rationale: A CSV import run's audit entry (catalog_audit_entries: csv_file, csv_import_number from 1 without gaps, source_commit, allowed_older_checkout, file_hashes, sources) records the files read with byte hashes, each CSV file's header line and every row's bytes, the current revision it left each part at, the parts earlier runs made that no row makes now (removed_parts), and the IDs of every import problem it found (new or already stored), whether or not it makes a Change. Every run sends exactly one catalog-csv source (database/<csvFile>.csv) and one substitutes-csv source; the route checks sha256(header + rows) against the file hash, refuses empty rows, and checks that every part's source row is one of those rows. A run is recorded (200 nothing_changed) whenever it read other files than the previous run of the same CSV file, even with no revision or problem, so the latest run always holds what the CSV says now; 422 noop only when nothing is new and the files are the same. A part an earlier run made that no row makes now gets a part-not-in-csv-file import problem whose detail does not name a run, so every later run finds it again; nothing is deleted. tooling/catalog-import zero_loss.rs rebuilds the CSV from the latest run (checking the recorded row count against the parsed rows, and file_hashes against the recorded files), matches rows by IPN (row problems by row number plus exact row bytes), accepts only import problems the latest run found (problems are shared by content, so an earlier run's problem must never explain a row) and none for two rows, compares each row with the revision that run left the part at (so later edits do not matter), reads supplier data from the run's rows, and matches incomplete-main-manufacturer-part problems by the row's own MPN and Manufacturer. A symbol keeps its revision when a neighbouring symbol in its library changes, so its stored source may name an older file hash and byte range: the report checks the blob against the whole symbol in the current file, and when the source names the current file it also checks the stored range. It checks 3D model references on the footprint revision the parts actually bind. Current revision sources are never used by the report.

title: CSV imports carry the current revision they expect per part, and the importer refuses an older checkout
rationale: ImportCommand carries the current revision it expects per part (parts[].expectedRevision, 0 for a part expected to be new) and the latest import run of its CSV file it read (expectedCsvImport, 0 if none); both are set only by ImportCommand::expecting(read_import_state), and the older-checkout setting only by allowing_older_checkout. These fields are private because each setter derives the correlation ID again from the import fingerprint plus all three, so re-running the same import after it applied gets a fresh comparison (422 noop) and re-sending an identical command replays. The same import with a different reason still gets 409 correlation_reused, as any reused ID for a different request does. If another import of the file landed in between, POST /api/catalog/csv-imports answers 409 newer_import_run; if any part's current revision differs, 409 conflict listing every such part and its current revision (the message names at most 10). Both write nothing and are not stored, like edit conflicts. read_import_state downloads only small fields (the fields= query; audit entries carry file_hashes, JSON [[path, sha]], for this). The server cannot run git, so tooling/catalog-import checkout.rs (used by services::prepare_import) checks the latest import run of every CSV file. If it came from a clean commit X, the import must be X or a descendant (git merge-base --is-ancestor; an import at Y+dirty counts as Y). If it came from X+dirty, the import must still be X or a descendant, and every file BOTH imports read (such as substitutes.csv or a shared symbol library; another CSV file does not count) must have the hash that run recorded or, for a descendant Y, must have changed in git between X and Y (git --literal-pathspecs diff --quiet X Y -- path), so a commit of the change still imports but a clean checkout, an unrelated later commit or other local changes cannot undo it. services::read_source_commit tells a missing git apart from a folder outside git, so the check says plainly when git is not installed. A commit the checkout lacks, files not read from git and recorded commits that are not 40 hex digits are refused too, one line per commit. allow_older_checkout skips the check and is recorded as allowed_older_checkout on the run's audit entry.

name: Blob hashing in the CSV import route: UTF-8 text through PocketBase, other bytes through JavaScript
description: $security.sha256 hashes text only. A blob whose bytes are UTF-8 (every real CAD file so far) is sent as text (blobs[].text) and the route hashes it with $security.sha256(text) and stores toBytes(text): both turn the same JS string into the same UTF-8 bytes, so the stored bytes are exactly the hashed ones (about 50 ms per MiB; invalid UTF-8 or lone surrogates become U+FFFD on both sides, so a false hash claim is refused). Other bytes are sent as base64 and decoded and hashed in pure JS (catalog_lib.js, about 3 s per MiB; the 60 s client timeout would fail near 20 MiB). Exactly one of text/base64 per blob. Passing a Go []byte or a JS array to $security.sha256 does NOT hash the bytes: goja stringifies it as '72,69,...'. The route sets $apis.bodyLimit(32 MiB) (PocketBase's default; above it PocketBase answers 413 or resets the connection while the client still sends), and submit_import serializes the body once and refuses one over IMPORT_BODY_LIMIT before sending. Measured on the real catalog: g-con (largest model, 1.5 MiB) 5.4 s -> 0.17 s; the 7 CSV files using all 13 models 14.4 s -> 0.67 s; largest request g-con at 1,900,969 bytes (1.8 MiB). An empty 3D model file is an empty-3d-model-reference import problem (file kept as a source), never a blob; the route still refuses empty blobs. Tests: tooling/catalog-import tests the_route_hashes_blob_bytes_exactly (both forms) and pocketbase_categories every_real_3d_model_imports_in_one_request_per_csv_file.

name: Catalog hook storage and shared code
description: Kept from mx-be5c16: canonical documents whose SHA-256 is their identity (revision snapshots) are stored in text fields with an explicit max (a TextField max of 0 means 5000), never json fields, so the hashed bytes round-trip. Shared hook code lives in a non-.pb.js file loaded with require(`${__hooks}/catalog_lib.js`) inside the handler; values used when registering a route (such as $apis.bodyLimit's limit) may be top-level consts of the .pb.js file.

title: Extra MPN columns, MPN TBC and unknown MPN columns become import problems; Excluded from BOM comes only from KiCad's own BOM flags
rationale: route_column: 'MPN' followed by digits (g-rfm MPN2) is ExtraMpn, 'MPN TBC' (g-rvr) is MpnToBeConfirmed, and any other header containing 'mpn' in any case ('MPN 2', 'Alt MPN', 'mpn2') is UnknownMpn; none goes into the part details. A non-blank MPN2 is an mpn-without-manufacturer import problem (detail: column, mpn, row_manufacturer) because a manufacturer part needs a manufacturer and nothing in the CSV says the row's Manufacturer makes it (Wurth 3670128 vs MS128-10F). MPN TBC is an mpn-to-be-confirmed import problem (detail: column, value): unconfirmed MPNs are not approved manufacturer parts. UnknownMpn values are unknown-mpn-column import problems (detail: column, value); no real CSV has one. Blank cells add nothing. PartDetails.excluded_from_bom (serde default, written only when true, last field; the edit route copies it from the current revision, so a rebinding edit keeps it and nobody can set it by hand yet) is true when a local symbol the part binds says (in_bom no), or every footprint choice is a local footprint with exclude_from_bom in its (attr ...). If only some footprint choices are marked (an unread KiCad-library choice counts as not marked) and the symbol is not, it stays unset and a footprint-choices-disagree-on-bom import problem keeps the choices. Notes and descriptions are never read. In the CSV catalog it is set for ART-0000-0001 only (g-art:TestPoint). ART-0001-0006 has no evidence either way: its symbol g-con:Conn_PIC_TagConnect_TC2030 is missing (missing-member) and its footprint is in KiCad's bundled library, which is not read. The g-no_bom libraries are all marked but unused. The zero-loss report checks all these rules (column table in zero_loss.rs, tests every_column_of_every_csv_file_has_one_destination and the_zero_loss_report_fails_when_its_new_checks_find_a_loss) and all 21 CSV files pass the pilot.
